samples.question: The picture is a cream board scattered with small decorative squares that mean nothing. Lying across the board is exactly one thin CORD: a single narrow route of straight horizontal and vertical runs that never crosses or touches itself. One black square CLAMP, larger than any decorative square, sits on the cord. On one side of the clamp the cord is TEAL and on the other side it is TAN. Sitting on the cord are large coloured BEADS, each a disc of red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple, and exactly one bead on the teal stretch wears a grey COLLAR ring. Only discs sitting on the cord are beads; every small square lying on the bare board away from the cord is decoration and means nothing, including decorative squares in teal, tan, black or any bead colour. The cord is folded at the clamp, and the fold pairs each point of the teal stretch with the point of the tan stretch that lies the same TRAVEL DISTANCE from the clamp, where travel distance means the length of the walk along the cord itself, following every corner and every detour hump, and never a straight-line distance. Measure the travel distance from the clamp to the collared bead along the teal stretch, then find the bead on the tan stretch whose travel distance from the clamp is the same. That bead is the FOLD PARTNER. Because the cord doubles back and its runs carry detour humps, the fold partner is never the tan bead that comes at the same place in bead order from the clamp, never the tan bead nearest the collared bead in a straight line, never the tan bead at the most similar height, never the tan bead in the most similar column, and never the first or the last tan bead along the cord. The partner's colour is worn by at least two beads in the picture and is never the single commonest bead colour, and the collared bead never wears it, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies it on its own. Find the fold partner of the collared bead. What is its colour? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
